```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(titleclassifier)
```

Many titles carry start/end dates for a position. **`remove_dates()`** detects
them, sets a `DATE.X` flag, and strips the date fragment.

```
remove_dates()
|
+- convert_ordinal()  1ST/2ND/3RD -> FIRST/SECOND/THIRD
+- has_date()         TRUE/FALSE: does the string contain a date?
+- remove_date()      strip 'YY, YY-YY, mm/dd/yyyy, month names, trailing numbers
```

## Examples

```{r}
x <- c("TREASURER (ENDED 3/16/23)",
       "DIRECTOR THRU 12/23",
       "SECRETARY UNTIL JAN 2023",
       "TRUSTEE (RESIGNED 1/24/23)",
       "PRESIDENT")

data.frame(title = x,
           has_date = has_date(x),
           cleaned  = remove_date(x))
```

Ordinals are spelled out first so later steps treat them consistently:

```{r}
convert_ordinal(c("1ST VICE PRESIDENT", "2ND LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR"))
```

**Input:** `TITLE_RAW` / cleaned title. **Output:** `TitleTxt2` (date-free text)
and the `DATE.X` flag. Continue with
[step 03](step-03-standardize-conj.html).
